statement: Whenever beautiful_pair(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, define d(a,b) = abs(nums1[a] - nums1[b]) + abs(nums2[a] - nums2[b]) for indices a,b. Then len(r) = 2, 0 <= r[0] < r[1] < n, and for every pair of indices (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < n, d(r[0],r[1]) <= d(i,j). Moreover, for every pair (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < n and d(i,j) = d(r[0],r[1]), the pair (r[0],r[1]) is lexicographically no greater than (i,j), meaning r[0] < i or (r[0] = i and r[1] <= j).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). The arrays satisfy len(nums2) = n, 2 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.

statement: On every input satisfying the preconditions, beautiful_pair(nums1, nums2) returns a result r: it does not fail, overflow, go out of bounds, or panic.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). The arrays satisfy len(nums2) = n, 2 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100000 and 0 <= nums2[i] <= 100000.
